summary: Sandstone light of 1881 at the northeast tip of Sand Island in the Apostle Islands; keeper Emmanuel Luick's family; automated 1921; National Park Service land today.

light.note: Focal plane: 52 ft (15.8 m) above lake level per NRHP; USLHS record gives 56 ft above water (17.07 m).

structures.note: Sandstone tower set into the corner of the one-and-one-half-story keeper's dwelling. 42 ft (12.8 m) per LighthouseFriends; USLHS record gives 37 ft (11.3 m) from base to lantern center; the NRHP gives no tower height.
48-foot steel skeletal tower beside the old light (LighthouseFriends); standing in 1977 (NRHP)

access.note: Apostle Islands National Lakeshore (NPS); reached by boat; a public dock at East Bay; a trail to the lighthouse. Several private cabins on the southeast corner.

visit.note: NPS: boat access; park volunteer lightkeeper posts give lighthouse tours (the NPS volunteer page does not name Sand Island).

facts.agency: US National Park Service (Apostle Islands National Lakeshore)

events.note: Construction begun June 6, 1880 under Louis Charles Lederle (LighthouseFriends); Congress funded it in 1880
Sandstone light, dwelling and tower; plans like Chambers Island and Eagle Bluff
Fixed white light first shown 25 September 1881 (LighthouseFriends); USLHS 1881

Steamer Prussia burned near Sand Island; no lives lost; crew rescued by the keeper. Dates differ: 12 September (LighthouseFriends, off the island); the Pioneer Press dispatch in the Superior Times says 'at 7 a. m. yesterday' (17 September), ten miles northwest of the light.
357 running feet of plank sidewalk relaid (Light-House Board)
Ore carrier Sevona struck a reef off Sand Island on 2 September 1905; seven lives lost
Island post office established (1911); discontinued 15 May 1916 (NPS)
Acetylene gas apparatus, 23 April 1921; first Apostle Islands light automated
Listed among lights where illumination was improved in fiscal 1921; flash changed (record gives Fl W 6s; LighthouseFriends says a flash every ten seconds)
Steel skeletal tower erected near the old light (LighthouseFriends); 1977 nomination describes it
Coast Guard removed the 1933 steel skeletal tower; light returned to the old lantern room (LighthouseFriends)

corrections.why: NPS site for Sand Island is part of Apostle Islands National Lakeshore; NPS volunteer and history pages describe the park's management of the island.
NRHP (1977) gives the focal plane as 52 feet above lake level (654 MSL): 15.8 m. Record's 18.3 m (ENC) and 17.07 m (USLHS, 56 ft above water) disagree; check the Light List datum before changing.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Lederle's end year: USLHS 1892, LighthouseFriends 1891 in its text and 1892 in its keeper list. Luick's end year: USLHS and LighthouseFriends 1920, NPS 1921. The NPS ties Luick's move to the 1921 automation.

LighthouseFriends: 12 September 1885, off Sand Island, keeper rescued the crew. Superior Times (Pioneer Press Bayfield dispatch dated 18 September): 'at 7 a. m. yesterday' (17 September), ten miles northwest of the light, no lives lost, crew rescued by the keeper. Unresolved; the story gives both.

resolved_conflicts.field: marriage of Emmanuel and Ella Luick
resolved_conflicts.explanation: NPS: 1896, when she was 16 and he 29. LighthouseFriends: 1886, in Rhode Island. Unresolved.

LighthouseFriends: struck a reef off Sand Island and broke in two. NPS quotation: the ship, trying to make York Island, was grounded on the reef. Unresolved; the story gives the NPS version as the NPS's own words.

USLHS: year discontinued 1933 and not an active aid; the 1977 nomination describes an automated light in the 1933 skeletal tower; LighthouseFriends says the Coast Guard removed the steel tower in 1985 and returned the light to the old lantern room. Whether the light shows today is not stated by any source read.
Tower: LighthouseFriends 42 ft; USLHS 37 ft base to lantern center. Focal plane: NRHP 52 ft (15.8 m) above lake level; USLHS 56 ft above water. Both differences are stated in the story.

notes_for_editor: Roster names from USLHS place record (NARA registers via Kraig Anderson); names as printed. The roster's acting-assistant headings for Ella G. Luick are as printed. The NPS says Luick's 1896 wedding date and his 1892-1921 service; LighthouseFriends says 1886 and 1892-1920. The 1885 Prussia fire rests on LighthouseFriends plus a single newspaper dispatch (Pioneer Press Bayfield dispatch printed in the Superior Times, 19 September 1885, page read directly); the dispatch's 'yesterday' gives 17 September, LighthouseFriends gives 12 September. The 1905 Sevona account: LighthouseFriends says off Sand Island; the NPS quotation says the ship tried to make York Island; both are in the story. The NPS quotation's source is not named by the NPS; the story does not call it the keeper's account. The 1905 newspapers (Washburn Times, Iowa County Democrat, 7 Sept 1905) were not read. Sand Island in the 1912-17 Bulletin index (Brown, Streckert, Gibbon) and the 1908 and 1915 Commissioner references are Sand Island, Alabama (Mobile Bay), not this station, and are not used. The NPS volunteer page does not name Sand Island; the story says so. Light characteristic: record Fl W 6s; LighthouseFriends says a flash every ten seconds; the 1921 Commissioner list gives no characteristic. Focal height: NRHP 52 ft above lake (15.8 m) vs records 17.07 and 18.3 m (USLHS gives 56 ft above water). Tower height: LighthouseFriends 42 ft; USLHS 37 ft base to lantern center. Two LighthouseFriends facts are passed on second-hand: the 1880 funding and the 1880 construction start, and the 1933 skeletal tower; no primary source was read for either. LighthouseFriends' 1985 removal of the steel tower is a single secondary source. The Bayfield County Press of 2 July 1881 (quoted by LighthouseFriends) was not used. Keeper and family details are from the NPS and LighthouseFriends; LighthouseFriends' full logbook excerpts are not reproduced beyond one sentence.
